cards.method: Reduced-form VAR (lag select + Granger + diagnostics + vec2var)
cards.when: 2-6 stationary series, frequentist VAR: IC lag selection, forecasting, Granger, residual diagnostics; vec2var bridges VECM->level VAR
cards.when_not: many series (-> #15/#12); a short sample that needs shrinkage; mixed frequency (-> #17/#18); structural shocks IRF/FEVD (-> #19)

alternatives.criterion: medium n or a short sample -> Minnesota shrinkage
large n -> factor structure
time-varying parameters/volatility
you want identified shocks (IRF/FEVD)

output_key_fields: selection/criteria: the suggested p per AIC/HQ/SC/FPE
stable: all(moduli(roots)<1) -- a critical post-check for reliable IRF/FEVD
fcst: list per variable fcst/lower/upper/CI (fan-chart data)
Granger/Instant: a flat record {statistic, p_value, parameter, method}
serial/arch/jb: residual-diagnostic records
interpretation_traps: Granger = predictive causality, NOT structural; H0='does not cause', p<0.05 -> predictive causality
the stability post-check (stable=True) is required before the IRF/FEVD can be trusted
diagnostics have H0='clean residuals': p<0.05 -> mis-specification (increase p)
the Granger test is problematic when the series are non-stationary

cards.method: Bayesian VAR (Minnesota prior)
cards.when: a multivariate VAR on a short/medium sample; hierarchical Minnesota shrinkage (GLP 2015); IRF by Cholesky or sign restrictions; posterior fan charts
cards.when_not: mixed frequency (-> #17); time-varying parameters or stochastic volatility (-> #14); very large n (-> #15); you want frequentist p-values (-> #11)

alternatives.criterion: you want an explicit Gibbs sampler + gir/sir IRF types
frequentist Granger/diagnostics, sample large enough
changing volatility/parameters

output_key_fields: acceptance_rate: MH tuning diagnostic (~0.20-0.40)
quants (bvar_predict): array [quantiles x horizon x variables], chart-ready
quants (bvar_irf): array [quantiles x horizon x impulse x response]
stable (bvar_companion): modulus<1
coef (bvar_summary): posterior median (not the MLE)
interpretation_traps: bvar_irf post-gate: an all-missing quants array -> sign/zero identification failed (stop); sign_restr is MxM with entries in {1, -1, 0, unrestricted}
coef is the posterior median, not a point MLE
the seed is mandatory: the sampler takes no seed argument of its own, so the wrapper seeds the generator before it runs

stationarity is methodological, NOT a hard gate: the Minnesota prior centres the 1st own lag at 1 (RW; the prior's own-lag mean b=1, fixed; the wrapper does not expose b) -> apply it to LEVELS/log-levels (typically I(1)), do NOT difference beforehand (differencing I(1) with b=1 = a de facto I(2) prior, over-shrinkage); the I(d) check is for cointegration awareness (I(1)&cointegrated -> consider a VECM, #23), not for differencing

cards.method: Bayesian VAR (Gibbs sampler)
cards.when: a Bayesian VAR with an explicit, transparent Gibbs pipeline (gen_var->add_priors->draw_posterior); flexible IRF/FEVD types feir/oir/gir/sir/sgir
cards.when_not: you want a ready-made hierarchical Minnesota prior, auto-tuned (-> #12); mixed frequency (-> #17); time-varying parameters or stochastic volatility (-> #14)

alternatives.criterion: hierarchical Minnesota + sign restrictions with minimal tuning
frequentist workflow + Granger

output_key_fields: fcst (bt_predict): one series per variable, [horizon x 3] lower/median/upper
irf: a series over horizons 0..h, [h+1 x 3] median + credible band
fevd: a series over horizons 0..h, [h+1 x n_vars]; rows sum to ~1
coefficients/sigma (bt_summary): posterior statistics
interpretation_traps: type: feir=non-orthogonalised; oir=Cholesky (order-dependent); gir=generalized (order-independent); sir/sgir=structural
the input must arrive time-indexed, not as a bare matrix
two MCMC seeds are consumed: one for the posterior sampler, one for the predictive draws
sources: Koop & Korobilis 2010, Bayesian Multivariate Time Series Methods for Empirical Macroeconomics (Foundations and Trends in Econometrics 3(4))

cards.method: TVP-VAR with Stochastic Volatility
cards.when: relationships/volatility change over time (TVP + stochastic volatility); posterior predictive distributions; IRF at each point in time t
cards.when_not: a small sample (heavily parameterized); constant coefficients (-> #12/#11); many series (2-4 variables in practice)

alternatives.criterion: constant coefficients suffice -> far cheaper
a general custom state-space TVP
discrete regimes -- CAUTION, #30 covers gaussian/linear only

output_key_fields: predict_density: {grid,value} -- the closure f(z) evaluated on a grid (cdf optional)
predict_draws: draws + quantiles (fan chart) + mean
irf: [draws x nhor] + bands [probs x nhor]; contemporaneous
parameter_draws: [draws x time] coefficient path (drift inspection)
interpretation_traps: the predictive density is a function, so it is never returned as such: it is evaluated on a grid
scenario: 1=no orthogonalization, 2=Cholesky(t) default, 3=DNP variant
requires save_parameters=True (always on) for sv_irf and sv_parameter_draws
tau is the LS-prior training split: ncol*p+1 <= tau < nrow

cards.method: Dynamic Factor Model / nowcasting
cards.when: many series with few common factors; nowcast with ragged edges/missing data (BM EM) and mixed frequency (quarterly_vars); rule-based r from Bai-Ng ICr
cards.when_not: few series (a VAR is more natural); you want a Bayesian mixed-frequency VAR with latent monthly states (-> #17); one low-frequency dependent variable from one high-frequency regressor (-> #18)

alternatives.criterion: you want a full Bayesian posterior + steady-state prior in mixed frequency
medium n, full VAR dynamics instead of a factor summary
one dependent variable, few high-freq regressors

output_key_fields: r_star (df_select_factors): a vector of length 3 (IC1/IC2/IC3, Bai-Ng); the IC table; the eigenvalues
factors (df_fit): T x r factors (QML/two-step/PCA); loadings C; transition A; the state and observation covariances Q and R
converged (df_fit): EM post-check (does not block)
X_fcst (df_predict): h x n nowcast/forecast in original units; F_fcst, the factors
R2 (df_summary): the share of variance the common component explains, per series
interpretation_traps: the 3 ICs often disagree; IC2 has the largest penalty -> the most parsimonious r (auto default)
factors/loadings are identified only up to rotation/sign (the factor sign has no absolute interpretation)
standardization happens INTERNALLY -> NO pre-scaling of the input
df_select_factors and the automatic r need an X with no gaps (PCA); an explicit r tolerates gaps (the EM route)

cards.method: Mixed-Frequency Bayesian VAR
cards.when: a Bayesian VAR with series of different frequencies (monthly indicators + quarterly GDP); nowcast with latent monthly states + a steady-state prior (Schorfheide-Song)
cards.when_not: all series at the same frequency (-> #12/#13); very large n (-> #15); one dependent variable driven by high-frequency regressors (-> #18)

alternatives.criterion: many indicators, factor nowcast (frequentist EM, faster)
you target one low-freq variable with few regressors
same frequency, no latent states

output_key_fields: forecast (mf_predict): a frame of variable/time/fcst_date/lower/median/upper, one record per row
log_mdd (mf_mdd): the log marginal data density (higher is better) for model comparison
mf_estimate: the prior/variance/aggregation echo, plus the fitted-model handle
interpretation_traps: Y is a list of series, monthly FIRST and quarterly last; gaps only at the end (the ragged edge)
aggregation='average' -> n_lags>=3
mf_mdd ONLY for variance='iw' (class _iw gate); ss->method{1,2}, minn->p_trunc(0,1)
the ss/ssng prior requires prior_psi_mean&Omega (or prior_psi_int); fsv->n_fac

cards.method: MIDAS regression (mixed data sampling)
cards.when: forecasting one low-freq variable (quarterly GDP) from high-freq regressor(s) (monthly/daily) through a parametric weight scheme (nealmon/nbeta/almonp)
cards.when_not: many interacting series / a system (the VAR family); nowcasting from many indicators (-> #17/#15); everything at the same frequency (ARDL, category 05)

alternatives.criterion: you want a mixed-freq VAR system + posterior + latent states
many high-freq indicators -> factor summary
same frequency, no weight scheme

output_key_fields: midas_coefficients (md_fit): the implied weights theta -- the shape over the high-frequency lags, and the interpretable part
converged (md_fit): NLS post-check (non-convergence is flagged, it does not block)
md_adequacy_test: a flat record {statistic, df, p_value, method}; H0 = the weight scheme is adequate
md_forecast: mean/lower/upper/level (newx of length h*m)
best (md_select): rule-based weight selection by AIC/BIC (not by the LLM)
interpretation_traps: md_adequacy_test H0='the restriction is adequate': p<0.05 -> REJECTION -> the scheme is wrong (Kvedaras-Zemlys)
the determining condition is length(x)==m*length(y); formula/data/start are built INTERNALLY (LLM safety)
start must have the right length per scheme: nealmon=3, nbeta=4, almonp=deg+1
NLS is deterministic for given start values -> no seed

cards.method: High-dimensional penalized VAR (structured penalties + rolling-CV lambda)
cards.when: a multivariate VAR with a large k·p relative to T (an OLS VAR over-fits); a structured VARX-L/HLAG penalty + rolling-OOS selection of lambda; a data-driven lag order (HLAG)
cards.when_not: a short sample wanting Minnesota shrinkage in levels with fan charts -> #12; frequentist Granger tests and p-values -> #11; a very large n with factor structure -> #15; mixed frequency -> #17

alternatives.criterion: a short sample, Bayesian shrinkage in LEVELS + posterior fan charts
a small k·p, you want frequentist Granger/IRF/diagnostics
a very large n with few common factors

output_key_fields: optimal_lambda: the best lambda (minimum in-sample MSFE); oos_msfe = the OOS MSFE on the test set (vs mean/RW/AIC/BIC)
coefficients: a k x (kp+1) sparse matrix (intercept + Y{i}L{l}); sparsity = the share of zeros
forecast (bvr_predict): a horizon x k path, built step by step; confint=True adds the lower/upper 95% band
model: the fitted producer handle -> bvr_predict / bvr_coef
interpretation_traps: stationarity: this estimator shrinks towards ZERO (MN=False by default, NOT a random-walk prior) -> apply it to STATIONARY data and difference I(1) series FIRST, the opposite of #12, which wants levels; I(1) and cointegrated -> consider a VECM, #23
the estimator DISCARDS the column names of Y: the variables come back as Y1..Yk by column order, consistently across fit/predict/coef -> map the positions in the frontend
struct: EFX is VARX ONLY (a pure VAR -> stop); HLAG*/Tapered are VAR-only; the non-convex MCP/SCAD are out of scope
the underlying predict returns only the final horizon (k x 1); the wrapper builds the full horizon x k path step by step
gran = c(penalty_grid_depth, number_of_lambda), two positive integers; too few rows for the rolling-CV window -> a clean stop (too few rows)
determinism: penalized (convex) + rolling/LOO CV = deterministic, no seed
sources: Nicholson-Wilms-Bien-Matteson 2020 JMLR 21(166) High-dim forecasting via interpretable VAR

cards.method: Hierarchical global-local shrinkage Bayesian VAR + stochastic volatility (HS/DL/R2D2/NG/SSVS priors, posterior fan charts + LPL)
cards.when: a multivariate BVAR (small to medium k) with global-local shrinkage that adapts sparse-vs-dense in a data-driven way (HS/DL/R2D2/NG/SSVS/normal on Phi) + stochastic volatility; posterior median/quantiles, predictive fan charts, LPL density forecasts
cards.when_not: a Minnesota random-walk prior in LEVELS with an IRF/FEVD toolkit -> #12; a frequentist penalized rolling-CV fit -> #142; time-varying coefficients -> #14; mixed frequency -> #17; a large-n factor model -> #15/#144; structural identification -> category 04 (bvs_irf is reduced-form)

alternatives.criterion: a Minnesota RW prior in LEVELS + a ready-made IRF/FEVD/companion/sign-restrictions toolkit
a frequentist penalized VAR-L, rolling-OOS lambda, deterministic (no posterior)
time-varying coefficients (TVP-VAR) + SV
reduced-form posterior impulse responses from the same fit

output_key_fields: phi_median: the posterior median Phi (K x M); phi_quantiles: an nq x K x M grid (2.5/25/50/75/97.5%)
convergence: n_retained/min_ess/n_stable/phi_finite/min_draws/ess_min/seed; converged + nonconvergence_reasons
model: the bayesianVARs_bvar producer handle -> bvs_predict/bvs_irf (register field=model, bucket=rds)
quants (bvs_predict): an nq x horizon x M predictive fan grid; mean: horizon x M; LPL and LPL_univariate when LPL=True (the density forecast)
irf_median (bvs_irf): M x shocks x horizon; irf_quantiles: nq x M x shocks x horizon (reduced-form bands)
interpretation_traps: stationarity: a prior mean of 0 shrinks towards ZERO (like #142, NOT a random-walk prior in levels like #12) -> use STATIONARY or growth data and difference I(1) series FIRST; precheck with ADF/KPSS

single-chain convergence: there is NO split-Rhat -> the gate is on the retained and stable draws, and DEGENERATE cases (an entirely blank ESS when the sampler is stuck, a non-finite Phi, zero stable draws) count as non-convergence; allow_nonconvergence overrides it (mirroring #68 and #61); a low ESS on TINY draw counts is NOT an error -> raise the number of draws

determinism: bvs_estimate and bvs_predict are stochastic and take NO seed argument of their own -> the seed is MANDATORY and the generator is seeded before the sampling (live-verified: seed=42 reproduces PHI exactly, and bvs_predict with seed=7 is identical); bvs_irf is deterministic

LPL: Y_obs must be the [ahead x M] realised values (a wrong dimension -> an upstream recycling warning; the wrapper blocks it); bvs_irf is reduced-form (shocks=1, no orthogonalization) -> structural shocks live in 04-structural-shocks
sources: Gruber & Kastner 2023 Forecasting macroeconomic data with Bayesian VARs: Sparse or dense? It depends! (arXiv:2206.04902)
Vehtari et al. 2021 Bayesian Analysis 16(2):667-718 rank-normalized ESS

cards.method: Sparse Dynamic Factor Model (EM with LASSO sparse loadings; arbitrary missing data / ragged-edge nowcasting; PCA/2Stage/EM/EM-sparse)
cards.when: large-panel nowcasting with interpretable sparse (LASSO) loadings + handling of arbitrary missing data; sdf_fit=a (sparse) DFM + imputation, sdf_predict=an h-step nowcast, sdf_factors=factor paths+covariances
cards.when_not: a dense factor model with Bai-Ng selection and explicit mixed frequency -> #15; a Bayesian mixed-frequency nowcast with bands -> #17; non-stationary data (difference it first); charts (the frontend); forecasting with err='AR1' (the prediction path breaks)

alternatives.criterion: you want DENSE loadings + automatic Bai&Ng factor selection + explicit quarterly_vars mixed frequency
a Bayesian mixed-frequency nowcast with posterior uncertainty/credible bands
an h-step nowcast/forecast (X_hat + F_hat) from the already estimated model

output_key_fields: factors: n x r factor paths; loadings: the p x r Lambda (zeros = a series that is irrelevant under EM-sparse)
var_explained/var_explained_cum: the share of variance (eigen-decomposition); eigenvalues
fitted: the n x p common component in the original scale; imputed: the balanced panel with the gaps interpolated (the nowcast input)
transition(A)/Sigma_u/Sigma_epsilon; converged/loglik/num_iter/alpha_opt(BIC-optimal); na_count
sdf_predict: X_hat (an h x p nowcast, columns=varnames) + F_hat (h x r); sdf_factors: factors + factors_cov (r x r x n)
interpretation_traps: err='AR1': the fit is valid BUT prediction is impossible (the shapes do not conform) — sdf_predict blocks it cleanly; use err='IID' for a nowcast
method='PCA' or '2Stage': no EM is run -> converged/loglik/num_iter/alpha_opt come back blank (NOT an error; it is a static or two-step estimate)
gate 1 <= r < ncol(X); the data MUST be stationary; standardization happens INTERNALLY (no pre-scaling); deterministic EM (no seed)
sources: Mosley, Chan & Gibberd 2023 (estimating dynamic factor models with sparse loadings, arXiv:2303.14125)
Banbura & Modugno 2014 (J. Appl. Econometrics 29:133-160, EM with arbitrary missing data)
Doz, Giannone & Reichlin 2011 (J. Econometrics 164:188-205, two-step); Bai & Ng 2002 (Econometrica 70:191-221, IC for r)

cards.method: High-dimensional mixed-frequency regression via MIDAS-ML sparse-group LASSO (Legendre/Gegenbauer weighted high-frequency blocks -> a low-frequency target, sg-LASSO lambda + mixing gamma, CV-tuned)
cards.when: Forecasting/nowcasting one low-frequency variable from MANY high-frequency indicators with many lags; each predictor (group) -> an orthonormal Legendre/Gegenbauer basis (degree+1) & a sparse-group LASSO for simultaneous group selection + within-group sparsity; gamma=the mixing weight (0 group-LASSO, 1 LASSO), lambda=the penalty (tuned with mml_cv).
cards.when_not: Few high-frequency regressors with an interpretable weight shape -> #18; factor structure or a large n -> #15/#144; a Bayesian mixed-frequency VAR with latent states -> #17; a same-frequency high-dimensional VAR -> #142; it is not multi-equation and has no IRF (a single low-frequency target).

alternatives.criterion: Few high-frequency regressors + an interpretable parametric weight shape theta (not sparse selection).
A large n; a latent factor structure summarises better than sparse selection.
A principled choice of lambda (lambda_min or lambda_1se) instead of the mml_fit path default, which is the smallest lambda.

output_key_fields: mml_fit: model (an 'mml_model' producer -> register field=model, bucket=rds); beta = (n_basis x nlambda) BASIS coefficients per lambda; the lambda/df/intercept path; n_groups/n_basis/gamma/degree/weight/s_default

mml_cv: lambda_min (minimising the CV error) and lambda_1se (the one-standard-error, more parsimonious choice); cvm/cvsd/cvupper/cvlower (the CV curve, chart data); nzero; beta_min/beta_1se + intercept_min/intercept_1se; seed (blank when unset)
mml_predict: fitted (length==nrow(newx)) + s + kind
interpretation_traps: mml_predict newx = the RAW high-frequency block (the same group/ncol as at fit time); the wrapper applies the SAME MIDAS transform internally — do NOT pass a pre-transformed design.
beta is in BASIS coefficients (Legendre/Gegenbauer functions), NOT per-lag weights; the per-lag shape = Psi %*% beta_group.
mml_fit (convex coordinate descent) is DETERMINISTIC (no seed); mml_cv partitions the folds RANDOMLY -> it REQUIRES a seed for reproducibility/caching (otherwise lambda_min fluctuates).
s: on a cross-validated model use lambda_min or lambda_1se; on a path model give a numeric lambda (the default is the smallest, that is the richest and least regularized model).
weighted basis: every group MUST have jmax >= degree+1 for a well-posed orthonormal basis; gamma ∈ [0,1] (the routine enforces it and the gate gives a clean message).
sources: Babii, Ghysels & Striaukas 2022 'Machine Learning Time Series Regressions With an Application to Nowcasting' JBES 40(3):1094-1106 (doi:10.1080/07350015.2021.1899933)
Babii, Ghysels & Striaukas 2021 (sparse-group LASSO with dependent/heteroskedastic data)

cards.method: Time-Varying-Parameter VAR with stochastic volatility + dynamic global-local shrinkage (triple/double gamma or ridge)
cards.when: A multivariate VAR (k>=2) where the relations EVOLVE smoothly over time (time-varying coefficients) AND the volatility changes (stochastic volatility), while MANY coefficients are in practice 0/constant -> dynamic shrinkage (triple/double gamma) automatically picks which ones are genuinely time-varying. The classic macro case: changing monetary transmission, structural breaks without explicit breakpoints.
cards.when_not: Constant (time-invariant) coefficients suffice -> #12/#11; time-varying parameters WITHOUT shrinkage but with explicit identification and IRF -> #14 (Primiceri); a single-equation TVP regression rather than a VAR -> #183; a high-dimensional penalized point estimate -> #142; nowcasting a panel with gaps -> #144.

alternatives.criterion: You want a TVP-VAR-SV with explicit Cholesky identification + structural IRFs (Primiceri), WITHOUT automatic variable selection.
The coefficients are plausibly constant -> a hierarchical Minnesota BVAR (cheaper, IRF/FEVD ready).
You want more aggressive shrinkage/sparsity (triple gamma) than the default double gamma; ridge = no selection.

output_key_fields: stv_estimate: model (the producer handle), converged/min_ess/retained_draws/n_varying_params (the convergence gate), variables/n_vars/p/mod_type/const
stv_forecast: quants (a named list per variable: a [probs x horizon] posterior predictive fan) + mean [variables x horizon] + probs/horizon
stv_tvp: paths (a named list per coefficient L<lag>.<var> & intercept: [probs x time] posterior bands) + coefficients/time/variable — the time-varying paths
interpretation_traps: Convergence: a single-chain sampler has NO split-Rhat; the gate is the minimum ESS over the beta_mean draws, IGNORING coefficients shrunk to constants (legitimate shrinkage, NOT poor convergence). A DEGENERATE entirely-blank ESS (every parameter constant) counts as NON-CONVERGENCE; it passes ONLY with allow_nonconvergence=True.
the seed is MANDATORY: without it the MCMC is not reproducible (the generator is seeded before the sampling).
SV is INHERENT (it is always a TVP-VAR-SV); there is NO sv toggle — the only shrinkage knob is mod_type. ONLY the VAR-coefficient draws are returned (not those of the variance-covariance).
the min_ess default (10) is a FLOOR for tiny-draw development; production runs (niter>=5000) must raise ess_min (>=200).
stv_tvp equation = the index of the TARGET equation (the response); the paths are the time-varying loadings of the lagged variables in it.
sources: Cadonna, Frühwirth-Schnatter & Knaus (2020), 'Triple the Gamma—A Unifying Shrinkage Prior..', Econometrics 8(2):20 (doi:10.3390/econometrics8020020)
Knaus, Bitto-Nemling, Cadonna & Frühwirth-Schnatter 2021 JSS 100(13) (shrinkage in the TVP model framework)

cards.method: Bayesian VAR & VHAR (Vector Heterogeneous AR; day/week/month long memory) with a Minnesota conjugate (analytic) / SSVS / Horseshoe prior + a posterior forecast fan
cards.when: multivariate Bayesian dynamics with shrinkage when the VAR is over-parameterized; bvh_var=a Bayesian VAR; bvh_vhar=a Corsi VHAR (day/week/month, multi-scale persistence); priors minnesota(conjugate/analytic)/ssvs/horseshoe(MCMC sparsity)
cards.when_not: the frequentist route with a sufficient sample -> #11; a hierarchical Giannone-Lenza-Primiceri prior without SSVS/HS/VHAR -> #12; a Gibbs sampler with generalized IRFs -> #13; time-varying parameters with stochastic volatility -> #14; mixed frequency or nowcasting -> #15/#17; structural IRF/FEVD -> category 04 (they are omitted here)

alternatives.criterion: a hierarchical GLP Minnesota without SSVS/HS/VHAR suffices
you want an explicit Gibbs sampler + gir/sir IRF types
time-varying parameters + stochastic volatility
frequentist Granger/diagnostics, the sample is sufficient

output_key_fields: model: the fit (a producer; the 'model' register field, a binary bucket); either an analytic Minnesota fit or an MCMC one
coefficients: the posterior mean, K x m (VHAR row labels a_day/a_week/a_month/const); pip: the inclusion probability (ssvs/horseshoe only)
converged/max_rhat/min_ess/nonconvergence_reasons: the convergence gate for the MCMC route; the analytic route reports converged=True with a blank Rhat
bvh_predict: forecast [n_ahead x m] point + lower/upper/se credible bands; draws + lower_joint/upper_joint (MCMC)
interpretation_traps: minnesota = an ANALYTIC conjugate NIW (closed form, no MCMC/convergence, the seed is optional); ssvs/horseshoe = MCMC (the seed is MANDATORY + a convergence gate + tiny draw counts)
convergence gate (mirroring #68): num_chains<2, or an entirely blank Rhat, is DEGENERATE -> non-convergence; max(Rhat)>rhat_max or min(Bulk_ESS)<ess_min -> stop unless allow_nonconvergence=True
the tiny defaults (num_iter=200) often do NOT meet strict thresholds -> the gate blocks conservatively (correctly); raise num_iter or override
nrow <= order_max+1 (VHAR: >23) -> a cryptic Eigen C++ assertion; gated explicitly
the predict level is a significance level (0.05 -> a 95% interval), NOT a confidence level; sparse=True gives SAVS coefficients (the MCMC route only)
sources: Corsi 2009 (HAR-RV, JFE); George-Sun-Ni 2008 (SSVS for VAR); Carvalho-Polson-Scott 2010 (horseshoe)
Vehtari et al. 2021 (rank-normalized split-Rhat + Bulk/Tail-ESS, Bayesian Analysis)

cards.method: PCA for MIXED I(0)/I(1) variables: an h-step-ahead OLS regression per series (a constant + p own lags) -> PCA on the RESIDUALS (Hamilton-Ma-Xi)
cards.when: common CYCLICAL factors behind many macro series whose stationarity is UNKNOWN or MIXED (I(1) levels + I(0) rates in the SAME panel); the method does NOT require the user to classify the series or to choose a per-series transformation — THE SAME regression on ALL of them; the defaults h=24/p=12 (monthly), h=8/p=4 (quarterly)
cards.when_not: ALL the series are demonstrably stationary and on a common scale -> classical PCA, #117; a latent factor with DYNAMICS, mixed frequency or a ragged-edge nowcast -> #15 or #144; charts (the frontend, §5); ONE series, since N>=2 is required; an unbalanced panel with gaps, since a balanced sample is required; isolating the cycle of ONE series -> the Hamilton regression filter (#57, category 10)

alternatives.criterion: ONLY when ALL the series are stationary; on non-stationary levels the standardization is undefined and the Bai-Ng criteria are corrupted (>1 factor at T=100 when the truth is 0)
you need a state-space DFM with factor dynamics, mixed frequency or ragged-edge missing data instead of a static PCA on the cyclical components

an effective T below 600, that is under 50 years of monthly data -> short_sample=True: a large h raises the risk of a spurious factor (Onatski & Wang 2021), and the paper recommends h=12, or h=1 in small samples
the series are ALREADY on a common scale and you want a COVARIANCE matrix; otherwise keep the default 'unit_variance' (= the paper's procedure)

output_key_fields: factor1/scores: the estimated common CYCLICAL factors per time point (T_eff x k) — the main chart-data; the x-axis = time
loadings: N x k sign-normalized (which series loads on which factor); loadings_hmx/factors_hmx = the paper's normalization (lambda'lambda/N = 1, f = N^-1 lambda'C, eq. 9-12)
sdev/var_explained/cum_var/pc1_var + pca_matrix ('correlation' under the default, 'covariance' under 'none')
residuals (T_eff x N) = the CYCLICAL COMPONENTS c-hat_it of eq. (7) + residual_sd/r_squared/sigma/rss/rank per series
coefficients (N x (p+1)) + lag_terms + residual_center/residual_scale: ALL the fitted params as NUMBERS (fit/apply externalization, §3b gate 6)
cor_residuals/eigenvalues/r2_eigen (eq. 18) + ic_p2/n_factors_icp2 (Bai-Ng IC_p2, eq. 19) + r_max_effective
h/p/n_obs/n_eff/df_residual/obs_index/time/frequency/recommended_h/recommended_p/short_sample/short_sample_threshold/short_sample_advice
interpretation_traps: DO NOT difference and DO NOT de-trend before the node: eq. (7) on LEVELS IS the transformation; pre-differencing transforms twice and destroys the cycle

NEVER standardize the raw series (the invalid step: under I(1) the population mean does not exist and the sample sd diverges with T); the scaling is applied ONLY to the (stationary) residuals and is an explicit gated option
scale_residuals='none' => var_explained (covariance) does NOT coincide with r2_eigen (eq. 18, ALWAYS the correlation matrix); read the pca_matrix field before comparing the two

a hard size gate: T >= h + 2p + 1, so that the effective T of T-h-p+1 is at least p+2; with fewer, the least-squares fit does NOT error — it returns residuals of EXACTLY 0 (silently wrong) and the PCA would then run on zeros
A DETERMINISTIC series (y_t = a + b*t, a running number, an index) makes the p lags collinear: the least-squares fit SILENTLY returns a deficient rank with blank coefficients — a hard gate here

a constant, zero-variance column makes the correlation return a blank with ONLY the warning «the standard deviation is zero» (silently wrong), and the scaled PCA report «cannot rescale a constant/zero column» — a hard gate here
p is ALSO the maximum order of integration/polynomial trend d_i <= p that is annihilated; the paper recommends p = the number of observations per year (persistent seasonality)
the signs of the PCs are arbitrary (the prcomp help Note) -> an explicit sign-normalization (the max-|loading| is positive); read the direction from the loadings

an effective T below 600, that is 50 years of monthly data, sets short_sample=True: an increased risk of a spurious factor. It is a DIAGNOSTIC, NOT a gate, since every h>=1 produces a stationary cyclical component
logs vs levels: the paper takes logs of whatever is described in rates of change (output/prices) and leaves rates/unemployment as they are — an UPSTREAM decision (cat 00), NEVER implicit here
outliers: the paper EXPLICITLY «make no corrections for outliers» for h=24 (h itself reduces the kurtosis); for extreme values see #246
sources: Hamilton, J. D., Ma, X. & Xi, J., «Principal Component Analysis for a Mix of Stationary and Nonstationary Variables», NBER WP 32068 (rev. 2026-04-08; econweb.ucsd.edu/~jhamilto/HX.pdf) — eq. (7) the regression, «Our procedure is to perform PCA on the regression residuals», «h=8/p=4 quarterly, h=24/p=12 monthly», §6.3 «Since c-hat_it is normalized to have unit variance», eq. (18)-(19) on the CORRELATION matrix, §5 «600 or larger»

Hamilton, J. D. (2018), «Why You Should Never Use the Hodrick-Prescott Filter», REStat 100(5) — the h-step-ahead regression as a trend/cycle decomposition; c_it is stationary for a polynomial trend d_i or I(d_i) with d_i <= p
Bai, J. & Ng, S. (2002), «Determining the Number of Factors in Approximate Factor Models», Econometrica 70(1) — IC_p2; Stock & Watson (2016, Handbook of Macroeconomics, p. 436) recommend it
Onatski, A. & Wang, C. (2021), «Spurious Factor Analysis», Econometrica 89(2), pp. 591-614 — why PCA on non-stationary levels produces spurious factors

cards.method: Nowcast news and revision decomposition
cards.when: attributing the change in a nowcast to each incoming data release -- the standard output of every central-bank nowcasting system
cards.when_not: there is only one vintage so there is no change to attribute; the model is not a state-space model and has no news structure

alternatives.criterion: attributing a nowcast revision to releases
attributing the nowcast LEVEL to variables
you only need the total revision

output_key_fields: news: the surprise component of each release
impact: the nowcast revision each release caused
weights: the Kalman gain applied to each series
revision_total: the sum, which must reconcile with the observed change
interpretation_traps: NEWS IS NOT THE RELEASE, it is the release minus what the model expected; a large release with no surprise moves the nowcast not at all
the impacts must sum to the total revision -- a residual means the decomposition is being applied across a model or specification change
revisions to previously published data enter as news too, and confusing them with new releases misattributes the move
sources: Banbura, Giannone, Modugno & Reichlin 2013, Now-casting and the real-time data flow (Handbook of Economic Forecasting 2A)

cards.method: Conditional forecasts and scenario analysis
cards.when: forecasting a system subject to a stated future path for some variables -- the standard tool for policy scenarios
cards.when_not: the conditioning path is inconsistent with the model's dynamics, where the implied shocks are implausibly large

alternatives.criterion: no scenario is imposed
the path must hold exactly
the path holds in distribution, within a band

output_key_fields: forecast: the conditional paths
implied_shocks: the shocks required to hit the conditioning path
shock_plausibility: how large those shocks are in standard deviations
unconditional: the baseline, for comparison
interpretation_traps: conditioning REQUIRES shocks to hit the path; if those shocks are several standard deviations the scenario is inconsistent with the estimated model and should be reported as such
which shocks are used to achieve the conditioning is not unique unless specified, and different choices give different paths for everything else
hard conditioning removes all uncertainty about the conditioned variables, which understates the fan for everything correlated with them
sources: Waggoner & Zha 1999 (Review of Economics and Statistics 81:639-651)
Banbura, Giannone & Lenza 2015 (International Journal of Forecasting 31:739)

cards.method: Factor-augmented vector autoregression
cards.when: many indicators carry information a small VAR cannot use, and factors extracted from them are added to the system rather than chosen ad hoc
cards.when_not: you have few variables, where a plain VAR suffices; the factors have no economic interpretation and the exercise needs one

alternatives.criterion: few variables and no information problem
hundreds of indicators to summarise
you want to keep the variables rather than compress them

output_key_fields: factors: the extracted factors and their loadings
irf: impulse responses of both factors and observed variables
variance_decomposition: contributions per shock
n_factors: how many were used and the criterion that chose it
interpretation_traps: factors are identified only up to ROTATION, so their individual interpretation requires an explicit normalisation that must be stated
the number of factors is a choice that materially changes the impulse responses; report the criterion and a robustness range
factors estimated from the full sample and then used in a recursive forecast exercise leak future information
sources: Bernanke, Boivin & Eliasz 2005 (Quarterly Journal of Economics 120:387-422)
Stock & Watson 2016, Dynamic factor models (Handbook of Macroeconomics 2A)

cards.method: VARMA and VARMAX estimation in state-space form
cards.when: the system has moving-average dynamics a pure VAR would need many lags to approximate, or exogenous variables that belong in the system
cards.when_not: a VAR with a moderate lag order fits adequately; the identification restrictions VARMA needs cannot be justified

alternatives.criterion: simpler, always identified, needs more lags
parsimonious when moving-average dynamics are genuine
exogenous variables and no moving-average part

output_key_fields: params: autoregressive, moving-average and exogenous coefficients
irf: impulse responses
converged: whether the likelihood maximisation actually converged
aic, bic, loglike
interpretation_traps: VARMA models are NOT IDENTIFIED without restrictions -- the same dynamics have many parameterisations, and estimation without them wanders
the likelihood is flat in many directions, so convergence is fragile and starting values matter a great deal
a VAR of sufficient order approximates a VARMA well; the parsimony gain is often not worth the estimation difficulty
sources: Lutkepohl 2005, New Introduction to Multiple Time Series Analysis, ch.11-12

cards.method: Bridge equations and unrestricted MIDAS
cards.when: linking high-frequency indicators to a low-frequency target without a full state-space system -- the workhorse of practical nowcasting
cards.when_not: you want a full system with news decomposition (-> dynamic factor); the frequency mismatch is so large that unrestricted MIDAS has too many parameters

alternatives.criterion: aggregate the indicator, then regress -- simple and transparent
few high-frequency lags, estimated freely
many lags, compressed by a weight function

output_key_fields: forecast: the low-frequency nowcast
params: indicator coefficients at each high-frequency lag
weights: the implied lag weighting
ragged_edge: how the incomplete final period was handled
interpretation_traps: the RAGGED EDGE is the whole problem: the final low-frequency period is incomplete and how the missing high-frequency observations are filled determines the nowcast
unrestricted MIDAS parameter count grows with the frequency ratio and overfits quickly; the restricted forms exist for that reason
aggregating the indicator before regressing discards within-period timing information that the nowcast could have used
sources: Ghysels, Santa-Clara & Valkanov 2004, The MIDAS touch (CIRANO Working Paper)
Baffigi, Golinelli & Parigi 2004 (International Journal of Forecasting 20:447)

cards.method: Large Bayesian VAR with dummy-observation priors, sum-of-coefficients and co-persistence
cards.when: the system has many variables and a flat-prior VAR would be hopelessly overparameterised; shrinkage makes it estimable
cards.when_not: the system is small enough for an unrestricted VAR; the prior cannot be justified and dominates the data

alternatives.criterion: the standard random-walk shrinkage
you want to discourage spurious deterministic trends
you want to allow cointegration without imposing it

output_key_fields: posterior: draws or moments of the coefficients
hyperparameters: the shrinkage actually chosen, often by marginal likelihood
irf: impulse responses with credible bands
forecast: predictive distribution
interpretation_traps: the SHRINKAGE HYPERPARAMETER dominates results in large systems; choosing it by marginal likelihood is defensible, fixing it by convention is not
the sum-of-coefficients and co-persistence priors are dummy observations, so they change the effective sample and must be reported
with many variables the prior contributes most of the information; calling the result data-driven is misleading
sources: Banbura, Giannone & Reichlin 2010 (Journal of Applied Econometrics 25:71-92)
Giannone, Lenza & Primiceri 2015 (Review of Economics and Statistics 97:436)

cards.method: Shadow-rate VAR consistent with the effective lower bound
cards.when: the policy rate is stuck at its floor, so a linear VAR treats a censored variable as if it moved freely and gets the transmission wrong
cards.when_not: the sample contains no lower-bound episode; a simple regime split is adequate

alternatives.criterion: no binding lower bound in the sample
the bound binds and you want one consistent model across regimes
you prefer explicit regimes to a latent shadow rate

output_key_fields: shadow_rate: the estimated latent rate, which goes negative at the bound
irf: responses that respect the bound
binding_periods: when the bound was active
params: VAR parameters on the shadow rate
interpretation_traps: the shadow rate is a LATENT construct and different estimators produce very different series -- comparing shadow rates across studies is usually comparing methods
impulse responses are state dependent when the bound binds; reporting one linear response is exactly the error the model exists to avoid
the shadow rate is not a policy instrument and should not be read as one
sources: Wu & Xia 2016 (Journal of Money, Credit and Banking 48:253-291)
Johannsen & Mertens 2021 (Journal of Money, Credit and Banking 53:1005)

cards.method: Sparse and regularised VAR via penalised multi-task regression
cards.when: the VAR has more parameters than observations and you want the data to select which lags and cross-effects matter
cards.when_not: the system is small; the sparsity assumption is untenable because everything genuinely depends on everything

alternatives.criterion: you want shrinkage without exact zeros
you want exact zeros and a sparse structure
you want whole lags or whole equations selected together

output_key_fields: coefficients: the sparse coefficient matrices
sparsity: share of coefficients set exactly to zero
lambda_selected: the penalty and how it was chosen
selected_structure: which lags and cross-effects survived
interpretation_traps: POST-SELECTION INFERENCE IS INVALID: standard errors computed on the selected model ignore the selection and are far too small
the penalty must not treat own lags and cross lags alike; own lags usually deserve less shrinkage and a uniform penalty distorts the dynamics
cross-validation on time series must respect the time order, or the selection leaks the future
sources: Nicholson, Matteson & Bien 2020 (International Journal of Forecasting 36:627)
